title: Close the headless-NUnit vs Unity-NUnit divergence gap so Unity-incompatible test constructs are caught by the primary gate
description:
Follow-up spun out of TASK-073. TASK-073 fixed a single symptom: the headless fast-tests csproj references NUnit 3.14.0 while Unity's Test Framework bundles an older NUnit (~3.5.x), so a test using Is.AnyOf (added in NUnit 3.6) compiled+passed headless but broke the ENTIRE Unity EditMode assembly (CS0117). The headless gate — our primary, fast, always-run gate — cannot catch this class of divergence, so it only surfaced during a manual Unity compile gate.

Goal: make the primary gate catch Unity-incompatible NUnit usage, so we do not rediscover this ticket-by-ticket. Options to evaluate (pick one in planning):
(A) Pin the headless test project's NUnit package version to match Unity's bundled NUnit exactly, so anything that compiles headless also compiles in Unity. Lowest ongoing cost; may lose newer NUnit conveniences.
(B) Add a periodic/CI Unity-compile check (batchmode -runTests or -quit compile) that runs the EditMode assembly through Unity's NUnit, catching divergence automatically. Higher infra cost; catches more than just NUnit (any Unity-API divergence).
(C) A lightweight static lint/grep denylist of known post-3.6 NUnit constructs (Is.AnyOf, etc.) in the headless gate. Cheap, but a denylist is inherently incomplete.

Investigate what NUnit version Unity's Test Framework actually bundles for this project's Unity version, decide (A/B/C or combination), and implement. Reference: the CS0117 was on Is.AnyOf; TASK-073's reviewer also noted Is.EquivalentTo at MicrogameDefinitionV2Tests.cs:262 is pre-3.6 (NUnit 2.x-era) and therefore SAFE — do not flag it as divergent.
acceptance_criteria: The exact NUnit version bundled by Unity's Test Framework (for this project's Unity version) is documented in the ticket or a repo note

A mechanism exists that would FAIL the primary (headless or CI) gate if a test uses an NUnit construct unavailable in Unity's bundled NUnit — via version-pinning (A), a Unity-compile CI step (B), a static denylist (C), or a combination
The chosen mechanism is demonstrated to catch the original failure: a test reintroducing Is.AnyOf is shown to be flagged/failed by the new gate (not silently passing headless)
The headless fast suite and the Unity EditMode assembly both remain green after the change
No false positives on existing safe pre-3.6 constructs (e.g. Is.EquivalentTo at MicrogameDefinitionV2Tests.cs:262 must NOT be flagged)

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
CLOSED (loop iter 7) — tests-after, depth FULL. All 5 ACs met; fresh-context review rev-t074 APPROVE-WITH-NITS (no HIGH / no MEDIUM); orchestrator fast-suite gate independently 849/0.

DELIVERY: static gate for the headless-NUnit vs Unity-bundled-NUnit divergence (rev-t073 follow-up). Commit f96620d (tests-after, single new file + csproj line + .meta). Fast 848->849 (+1 the gate test).

OPTION CHOICE (investigated all three, ruled out A/B with hard evidence): AC1 — Unity's bundled NUnit is EXACTLY 3.5.0.0 (com.unity.test-framework 1.4.6 -> com.unity.ext.nunit 2.0.5 -> nunit.framework.dll AssemblyVersion 3.5.0.0, read from the actual DLL, documented in the class doc). OPTION A (pin headless NUnit to 3.5.0) RULED OUT with evidence: it compiles clean (proving no post-3.5 construct remains in the 849-test suite beyond the already-removed Is.AnyOf) BUT throws TypeLoadException at runtime under net8.0 — NUnit 3.5.0 is net40/45-only (netstandard landed ~3.7), so legacy remoting/System.Web types are absent; pinning down would take the suite 849->0. No single NUnit version both net8.0-loads AND matches Unity's 3.5.0 surface, so exact-match pinning is genuinely infeasible. OPTION B (Unity-compile CI) RULED OUT: no Unity license/runner in this CI env (documented in .github/workflows/fast-tests.yml:13). LANDED ON OPTION C: a static denylist analyzer test (NUnitUnityCompatibilityTests.cs) mirroring the existing GDD §13 System.Random source-scanner pattern — textual scan (StripComments removes //, /* */, AND string literals so it's self-scan-safe) over Assets/Tests/EditMode + PlayMode (SearchOption.AllDirectories), fail-loud path resolver (walks up trying BOTH repo-root and Unity-CWD layouts, THROWS if not found — no TASK-075 CWD-vacuity fragility).

REVIEW (verified firsthand): regex precision both directions — \bIs\.AnyOf\b matches Is.AnyOf, NOT Is.EquivalentTo (now MicrogameDefinitionV2Tests.cs:316) / Is.All.Not / Has.None / substrings; live non-vacuous [Test] asserting offenders Is.Empty, scans real files via File.ReadAllText. AC3 demonstrated: reintroducing Is.AnyOf into SmokeTests.cs failed the gate naming the file+construct, reverted byte-identical. AC4 both green: headless 849/0; Unity ran the new test 1/1 via filtered MCP run_tests against the real bundled NUnit 3.5.0 (single-file+csproj change = negligible regression surface). AC5 no false positive on Is.EquivalentTo.

[ASSUMED] (reviewer-confirmed sound): denylist scoped to the single confirmed incident (Is.AnyOf) rather than a speculative post-3.5 construct list — avoids inventing false-positive risk; class doc documents the inherent incompleteness + the extension path (add an entry per real future divergence).

DEFERRED LOW-1 (trivial, opportunistic — NOT swept): NUnitUnityCompatibilityTests.cs:75 class-doc cites the old Is.EquivalentTo line :262; actual is :316 (the commit body has it right). Cosmetic doc line-ref only, no behavioral impact; sweep on next touch of that file.
